text:
aanika-peopleops: Quick thread — offer accepted for Rohit (starts 06/30) but he's still overseas waiting for H-1B visa stamping. USCIS approved petition (I-797) but consulate appointments in Mumbai are ~8 weeks out. Need to confirm hiring/legal/payroll next steps. Can counsel advise on whether we can start him remotely from India and what benefits/payroll look like?

rohit: Hey all, thanks. I can start doing ramp-up work from India (no US pay) before I land. Goal is to arrive in the US by mid-July after stamping. Happy to be flexible.

marta-legal: Hi @aanika-peopleops and @rohit. Short answer: we cannot employ him as a US W-2 employee performing US work while he's physically outside the US without proper payroll setup; similarly, we cannot put him on US payroll while he's abroad except under specific local employer-of-record arrangements. Two paths:
- Option A: delay US employee start until he physically enters the US with H-1B stamp and completes Form I-9 (in-person or remote as allowed).
- Option B: engage him as a contractor or through an EoR in India for the interim (commercial/legal/privacy review required).

marta-legal: Also checklist for H-1 stamping arrival: bring original I-797, passport, appointment confirmation, employer support letter (we have a template), and recent pay stubs once he starts in US. We'll produce a short onboarding letter for the consulate.

ken-payroll: From payroll perspective: if he is on contractor/EoR in India, benefits (medical, 401k) and taxes differ. For US W-2 hires, benefits enrollment windows start on official US start date. If start delayed, COBRA/benefits eligibility will shift. Payroll needs final hire date to create payroll record and W-4.

aanika-peopleops: Noted. We don't want to lose him by delaying. What's the minimum legal paperwork to allow him to do unpaid, pre-hire onboarding work (e.g., reading docs, shadow calls)?

marta-legal: He can do unpaid orientation/pre-reading as long as it's truly unpaid and not productive work. However, unpaid work has risks and must be limited to non-assignable tasks. We'll draft a checklist of safe activities.

rohit: I can do onboarding modules, shadowing, and knowledge transfer sessions that are unpaid until stamp is done. Thanks.

liam-it: For IT: if we delay US start but still want Rohit to have a laptop, we can either: ship to his India address (need exec approval for international shipment and customs) or hold provisioning until US address is confirmed. Shipping internationally can delay delivery and may block some device enrollment profiles. Thoughts?

aanika-peopleops: Prefer to hold hardware in US to avoid customs/hardware loss. Can we do cloud access (non-production) for ramp-up without shipping secure laptop?

liam-it: Yes, we can grant limited cloud/dev env access via SAS token and VPN split-tunnel rules, but we can't give access to production secrets until he is on US payroll and passes background check.

ken-payroll: Background check vendor requires signed consent and identity docs; they can run while he's overseas in some countries, but results can be delayed. Payroll needs SSN or ITIN to create pre-hire record — SSN only after he lands and gets Social Security card. We can create a placeholder record but cannot pay him on US payroll until SSN is available.

marta-legal: Two more practical items: (1) we should issue a conditional offer letter that states start contingent on visa stamping and I-9 completion; (2) we'll prepare a consulate support letter and appointment checklist.

aanika-peopleops: I'll update the offer to be "start contingent on valid US work authorization and arrival" and share the consulate letter draft. Rohit, please upload scanned I-797 and passport copy to secure upload link: https://onboard.redwood.ai/upload (choose "visa docs").

onboard-bot: Document upload received: I-797.pdf, passport_rohit.pdf. Status: pending legal review.

marta-legal: Got the docs. I'll generate the employer support letter and send via email. For timeline: consulate delay may push start ~62d8 weeks; if that's unacceptable we can evaluate short-term EoR.

ken-payroll: If we go EoR, legal + finance need 72h to evaluate costs. Please flag ASAP if team wants that route.

aanika-peopleops: Team decision: try to preserve the start but do unpaid ramp-up remotely and hold benefits until US start. If consulate pushes beyond 8 weeks, we'll revisit EoR. I'll confirm by EOD.

rohit: Okay — will proceed with unpaid onboarding tasks and await the consulate letter. Thanks everyone.

marta-legal: One final note: do not travel to the US on B-1/B-2 to start work. That is not permitted. Use H-1B stamp only.

aanika-peopleops: Will keep thread updated. Marking as in-progress. \"
